instruction.text: What do all these animals have in common? Choose the correct answer.
Read the text and fill in the gaps to find out what all mammals have in common.

atoms.sound: All mammals are warm-blooded. That means, that their core temperature always stays the same and does not adapt to the temperature of their environment. Humans, for example, normally have a body temperature of 37 °C
atoms.b: All mammals are ((++warm-blooded cold-blooded)). That means, that their core temperature always ((++stays_the_same changes)) and ((++does_not does)) adapt to the temperature of their environment. Humans, for example, normally have a body temperature of ((++37_°C 100_°C)).

atoms.sound: All mammals have some kind of hair. Some mammals have thick fur, while others have small, scattered hairs. Hair serves to protect animals from cold and injury.
atoms.b: ((Some ++All)) mammals have some kind of hair. Some mammals have thick ((noses ++fur)), while others have small, scattered hairs. Hair serves to protect animals from ((++cold_and_injury poison)).

atoms.sound: All newborn mammals are breastfed milk by their mothers. Most mammals care for their young intensively. They accompany their offspring for the first weeks, months or sometimes years, until they can look after themselves.
